hardening.title: v3.0.x — Validation and release hardening
hardening.goal: Prove and protect the shipped 3.0 surface before broadening it. Patch releases contain fixes, fixtures and evidence; additive APIs move to 3.1.
hardening.exit: P0 merge/normalization/archive risks resolved with negative tests; a licensed native fixture corpus and explicit rendering matrix published; supported release artifacts install and pass their declared platform tests.

operations.title: v3.1.0 — Operational confidence
operations.goal: Make server diagnostics, CLI automation, contracts and public API results reliable and complete.
operations.exit: Unknown and partial results are explicit; drift matching is identity based; paginated REST/GraphQL data and job outcomes are covered; API/CLI workflows, versioned reports and upgrade docs are exercised.

authoring.title: v3.2.0 — Native authoring and accessibility
authoring.goal: Expand authoring only through native fixtures and target-version rendering evidence.
authoring.exit: Supported dashboards, panes, calculations, formatting and templates survive native save/reopen; accessibility reports distinguish static evidence from required rendered checks.

scale.title: v3.3.0 — Fleet scale and governed promotion
scale.goal: Scale local workflows and deploy workbook changes with reviewable plans, bounded resources and recoverable operations.
scale.exit: Benchmarks and resource budgets published; cross-platform interruption recovery demonstrated; promotion previews, permissions, revision checks, job outcomes and rollback limits documented and tested.

research.title: Research backlog — Evidence and interoperability
research.goal: Run bounded experiments before committing expensive or uncertain capabilities to a release. No delivery date or version commitment.
research.exit: Each spike produces representative inputs, a reproducible result, explicit limits and a go/no-go decision. A production feature requires a separately scoped implementation issue.

items.title: Establish Tableau Desktop/Server rendering acceptance matrix
items.baseline: 3.0 XML/package and Hyper tests pass; docs/engineering-validation.md explicitly leaves Desktop/Server rendering acceptance unverified.
scope: Build an opt-in licensed Desktop and test Server/Cloud harness with a manual evidence path where automation is unavailable.
Cover joins, relationships, independent panes, dual axes, quick calculations, formatting and extract-backed publishing by actual target version.
acceptance: Record OS, Tableau build, feature, fixture hash and evidence for every tested cell.
Native open, save/reopen and rendered field/axis behavior pass for each claimed supported feature.
Untested, unsupported and failed cells remain explicit; publish a reproducible manual checklist and test-artifact policy.
items.exclude: Do not infer renderability from valid XML or promise universal Tableau-version support.

items.title: Promote native workbook corpus into reproducible CI fixtures
items.baseline: Tracked fixtures are small XML samples; the 11-workbook round-trip corpus used for 3.0 includes locally stored, ignored TWBX files. Its coverage is not reproduced by an ordinary CI checkout.
scope: Select anonymized redistributable native TWB/TWBX samples across supported versions and XML patterns, with license/provenance and expected diagnostics.
Include unknown XML/comments/PIs, named connections, multiple sources, nested assets and complex authoring.
acceptance: A clean checkout fetches or contains every declared fixture with pinned hashes and documented redistribution rights.
CI runs XML/asset round trips, patch convergence and expected semantic diagnostics for the corpus.
Known source defects are fixture expectations rather than suppressed checks; report coverage by version and feature.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Expand supported platform, extras and release artifact checks
items.baseline: CI exercises Python 3.11-3.13 on Linux, real Hyper and an installed core wheel. Local Apple Silicon Hyper testing needed a documented pantab executable substitution.
scope: Test supported optional extras and core wheels/sdists across a declared Linux/macOS/Windows matrix; verify published dependency compatibility.
Evaluate newer Python versions as experimental until evidence supports adding them; validate metadata, packaged templates and reproducible provenance.
acceptance: Every supported environment installs official dependency binaries and runs representative workflows without hidden patches.
Unsupported architecture/runtime combinations fail with actionable guidance and are documented.
Build/Twine checks, source exclusions, installed-wheel imports and trusted-publish artifact checks are release gates.
items.exclude: Do not claim all platform combinations or a newer Python runtime are supported before their tests pass.

items.title: Bound and validate archive/XML resource consumption
items.baseline: Entity/network protections exist. PackageManager currently delegates archive extraction to zipfile.extractall without a project-level member/count/size policy.
scope: Audit member normalization, duplicate/case-colliding paths, symlinks, nesting and expanded-size limits; define safe limits and cleanup behavior.

Define plain-TWB/XML byte, depth and node budgets, enforced incrementally or before excessive allocation across default and strict modes; huge_tree parsing and post-parse checks are not resource limits.
Add adversarial XML/ZIP corpus cases and connector-aware secret redaction in diagnostics without leaking credentials.
acceptance: Reject or explicitly handle ambiguous/path-colliding archive members before installing files.

Tests cover malformed XML/ZIP, valid but oversized/deep XML, node budgets, traversal, oversized expansion, many members, failure cleanup and destination preservation; assert bounded memory/termination behavior.
Document threat model, resource limits and any compatibility overrides; preserve safe unknown XML.
items.exclude: No claim of a reproduced exploitable traversal bug solely from use of zipfile; findings require concrete tests. New configuration APIs belong in a minor release.

items.title: Make workbook merge reconcile identities, references and assets
items.baseline: Workbook.merge() exists, but its collection-copy implementation suffixes conflicting names without a complete identity/reference/asset rewrite plan. Legacy issue #51 is closed.
scope: Define dry-run collision reports and deterministic identity maps for datasources, fields, sheets, dashboards, actions and packaged assets.
Either reconcile an explicitly supported collision or fail before mutation; make mutation transactional and respect the supplied conflict policy.
acceptance: Duplicate IDs/names, repeated collisions and overlapping asset paths produce deterministic outcomes with no dangling references.
Merged dependencies and owned extract/image assets survive save/reopen; rollback restores both input states on failure.
Native acceptance covers supported merged layouts and limitations are explicit.
items.exclude: Do not silently reinterpret ambiguous shared datasources. A new merge API is scheduled in a minor release; patch releases may reject unsafe existing cases.

items.title: Harden server transport, pagination, authentication and job outcomes
items.baseline: ServerClient provides PAT/credentials, publish/download, refresh and TSC upload delegation. list_workbooks() reads one page; transport/job policy is limited.
scope: Use TSC pagination and version-aware adapters; expose job wait/status, timeout/cancellation and structured transport errors.
Design supported Connected Apps authentication, session lifecycle, site scoping and redacted diagnostics; bound retries and prevent blind publish retries.
acceptance: Tests cover multi-page inventory, expired auth, permission errors, rate limits, timeout and async failure/cancellation.
An uncertain publish result cannot automatically create duplicate content; outcomes include job and server identity.
Opt-in live contract tests cover the declared REST/TSC versions and supported authentication modes.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Make Metadata API queries paginated, schema-aware and completeness-aware
items.baseline: MetadataClient exposes raw queries and small templates; it does not aggregate connection pagination or interpret GraphQL errors/partial results.
scope: Validate query templates against declared Tableau schemas and stable LUID identities; paginate supported connection types.
Preserve errors, permission filtering, disabled metadata, throttling and incomplete-result evidence in typed outcomes.
acceptance: Mock fixtures cover data plus errors, permission-filtered results, page cursors and schema differences.

Every outcome records principal, site, permissions mode and declared visibility scope; empty within visible scope is distinguished from unavailable/incomplete evidence. Site-wide completeness requires independent evidence and otherwise stays unknown.
Optional live queries pass against supported deployments; tokens are redacted and bounded query/retry controls are documented.
items.exclude: A successful HTTP response does not establish complete GraphQL data. See official Metadata API common-errors documentation.

items.title: Complete local/published drift reports with explicit unknown states
items.baseline: ServerClient.detect_drift() currently compares server addresses and returns [] on lookup failure. It does not fulfill the broader original #102 scope.
scope: Reconcile stable workbook/datasource/connection identities and compare published XML/metadata, connection attributes, schema and version evidence.
Report extract freshness from accessible job/refresh evidence with observation time, configured freshness threshold and completeness state; keep reads side-effect free.
acceptance: Typed reports distinguish clean within evidenced visibility scope, drifted, partial and unavailable results; failures or permission-filtered emptiness never masquerade as site-wide no drift.
Tests cover duplicate captions/hosts, missing sources, partial permissions, stale refresh evidence and schema/version differences.
JSON/text/CLI reports identify evidence source and timestamp; sensitive values are redacted and no mutation occurs.
items.exclude: Do not equate a failed refresh with a proven data-age violation or compare every local connection against every server connection.

items.title: Expose 3.0 workflows through CLI and versioned JSON schemas
items.baseline: The API contains snapshot patches, scoped impact, compatibility, durable manifests and extract contracts; CLI/report coverage is not a single stable contract.
scope: Define CLI parity for patch create/apply, impact, compatibility, manifest prepare/apply/resume/rollback and extract contract validation.
Version patch/manifest/report schemas and specify exit codes, dry runs, output paths and backward-compatible readers.
acceptance: Core workflows run from an installed package without optional integrations; integration commands identify required extras.
Machine-readable output validates against published schemas and never mixes logs into JSON stdout.
Negative CLI tests cover stale inputs, missing extras, invalid manifests, ambiguous identities and configuration errors.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Add reviewable extract schema-change plans and provenance
items.baseline: ExtractContract already validates table identity, types/nullability/keys and strict/additive/replace writes with explicit backfills.
scope: Provide serializable dry-run plans for schema changes and compatible XML metadata updates, with input hashes and chosen backfill policies.
Record table/schema identity, source/destination hashes, row counts, write policy and caller-supplied provenance without exposing source data.
acceptance: A prepared plan validates before mutation and rejects changed inputs or unsupported loss of information.
Add/drop/backfill/replace and unrelated-table preservation are covered with exact decimal/time/null/key cases.
Contract errors and provenance reports use the stable JSON/CLI surface; documented examples show inspect-plan-apply-verify.
items.exclude: Do not weaken the exact type checks or imply arbitrary database migrations are supported.

items.title: Unify governance findings and CI report formats
items.baseline: GovernanceRuleset, compliance/contract runners and JUnit output exist. A complete shared schema, source locations and all historical SARIF/annotation promises are not established by closed #107.
scope: Define shared findings with stable rule IDs, datasource-qualified identity, XML location, severity and evidence.
Support versioned JSON, validated JUnit/SARIF and safe GitHub annotations, with configurable baselines and severity policy.
acceptance: Format fixtures validate against their declared schemas; tests cover escaping, multi-file locations and stable ordering.
Exit codes distinguish findings, configuration failure and unavailable checks; baseline entries expire visibly.
One issue retains the same identity and severity across library, fleet and CLI reports.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Make agent discovery and mutation plans consistently typed and bounded
items.baseline: describe(), capabilities(), OperationReceipt and transaction helpers exist; newer workflows expose separate report/plan shapes.
scope: Expose content-based, version-aware capabilities with installed-extra and supported-operation evidence.
Add inspectable mutation plans/receipts that compose patches, contracts and migration reports; limit payload size and redact secrets.
acceptance: Typed schemas distinguish proposed, applied, rejected, unavailable and partially supported operations.
Read-only discovery never mutates XML/assets and bounded summaries identify omitted content.
Examples and negative tests demonstrate stale plans, ambiguous fields and unavailable integrations with actionable receipts.
items.exclude: No autonomous approval bypass, hosted agent service or mandatory external AI dependency.

items.title: Complete native dashboard layout, device-layout and action authoring
items.baseline: Dashboard zone/action reads and basic moves/add/remove methods exist. Native responsive layout generation and broad action semantics remain limited despite closed #114.
scope: Support nested containers, explicit desktop/phone/tablet layouts and source/target/trigger/field mapping for supported actions.
Preserve stable IDs, style/device inheritance and unknown XML; reject unsupported structures rather than flattening them.
acceptance: Fixtures cover nested layout moves, action remapping, device layout edits and field dependencies with save/reopen.
Desktop/Server evidence proves supported action triggers, sizing and device selection.
Builder/spec parity, rollback and limitations are documented with runnable examples.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Expand worksheet authoring with explicit multi-source and table-calc semantics
items.baseline: 3.0 authors native panes/dual axes and quick table calculations for one datasource per worksheet; inspection can resolve multi-source references.
scope: Design explicit primary/secondary source relationships, axis bindings and aggregation constraints without relying on captions.
Expand addressed/partitioned/window calculations and pane-specific sorting/filtering only from native fixture evidence.
acceptance: Valid multi-source and invalid ambiguous cases are represented by fixtures and deterministic validation errors.
Rendered output and native save/reopen agree for each supported pane/axis/calculation combination.
The existing one-source builder remains compatible; unsupported blends are clearly reported.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Publish a rendering-verified template gallery and recipes
items.baseline: The package ships ten TWB templates and TemplateEngine mappings. File presence and XML tests alone do not establish visual acceptance.
scope: Create a versioned template manifest with field/role/type contracts, feature requirements and native rendering evidence.
Include relationships, extracts, pane/axis examples and dashboard layouts with screenshots or equivalent acceptance records.
acceptance: Every advertised template passes installed-wheel creation, complete mapping, semantic validation and native save/reopen.
Incomplete/incompatible mappings fail before output installation; native field identities survive remapping.
Publish clear core/Hyper/Server recipes and regenerate evidence when templates or supported versions change.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Implement evidence-based accessibility diagnostics and rendered checks
items.baseline: Issue #111 remains open; there is no accessibility module in the 3.0 source tree. Its old draft mixed WCAG criteria with Tableau-specific heuristics.
scope: Implement checkable XML diagnostics for text/background contrast where known, image/viz alternatives, labels and color-only encoding risks.
Separate static findings from manual or rendered keyboard/focus/screen-reader checks; use Tableau version-specific guidance and exact WCAG mappings.
acceptance: Reports distinguish pass, fail, unknown and manual-review-required with evidence, criterion and remediation.
Contrast tests use the WCAG luminance calculation and appropriate thresholds for the actual text case.
Mark-count advice is a Tableau rendering heuristic, not a WCAG success criterion; XML-only results never certify WCAG AA compliance.
A rendered acceptance checklist and API/CLI reports cover representative accessible and inaccessible examples.
items.exclude: Do not claim XML establishes keyboard/screen-reader behavior or full WCAG conformance. Formal audits require the rendered published experience.

items.title: Extend formula grammar, versioned functions and scoped AST analysis
items.baseline: A Lark parser, AST, function registry and linter exist. The complete language and per-version signatures are not proven by those modules alone.
scope: Build a native-formula corpus including LODs, escaped identifiers, table/window calculations, comments and external SCRIPT/RAWSQL calls.
Resolve AST references through the scoped graph; record unsupported syntax/functions and versioned signatures rather than guessing return types.
acceptance: Corpus reports show parse coverage and expected unsupported cases; no parse failure becomes a clean analysis result.
Regression tests cover source-qualified collisions, nested scopes and string/comment preservation.
Lint diagnostics distinguish syntax, semantic uncertainty, deprecation and performance heuristics with source locations.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Verify native formatting, palette inheritance and conditional encoding
items.baseline: Theme, palettes and FormatSpec read/write exist. Conditional encoding and inherited defaults need native interpretation rather than generic XML injection.
scope: Define supported worksheet/dashboard/field formatting inheritance and connector/version-specific capabilities.
Add validated conditional encodings, palette bindings, font/number/date formats and label styles where native fixtures support them.
acceptance: Formatting read/apply round trips preserve unrelated styles and unknown format nodes.
Native rendering validates each supported palette/inheritance/conditional encoding case.
Specs, builders and theme application produce equivalent supported output and unsupported requests fail explicitly.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Strengthen migration durability and cross-platform interruption guarantees
items.baseline: MigrationManifest already has exact prepared outputs, hashes/backups, process recovery, file fsync and advisory POSIX/Windows locks. Fleet installation remains per-file.
scope: Fault-inject file replacement, journal updates, backup reads and multi-process contention on supported filesystems/platforms.
Define directory-sync, permissions/metadata retention and storage budget policies; provide explicit limits for network filesystems and power loss.
acceptance: Cross-platform tests prove resume/rollback after each declared interruption point and reject external changes.
Backups and manifests survive the tested durability model; lock acquisition/cleanup is deterministic.
Document guarantees separately for process interruption, power loss and whole-fleet atomicity; do not overstate the latter two.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Benchmark and scale fleet workflows with bounded concurrency
items.baseline: FleetScanner and migration/compliance operations exist, but the release does not publish large-corpus throughput or memory budgets.
scope: Benchmark parse, diff/patch, validation, extract and fleet tasks by workbook/XML/asset size with reproducible environments.
Design bounded worker pools, cancellation, incremental results and safe cache invalidation without shared writable workbook handles.
acceptance: Publish baselines and explicit target budgets before optimizing; fail meaningful regressions in dedicated performance checks.
Serial/parallel reports and mutation outputs agree; tests cover cancellation, corruption and worker failure.
Peak memory, temporary disk use, file handles and Hyper process counts remain within documented configured limits.
items.exclude: Do not promise gigabyte DOM parsing or infer speed gains from synthetic tiny fixtures alone.

items.title: Add incremental scoped indexing and cross-workbook lineage
items.baseline: WorkbookIndex is a SQLite field/connection catalog keyed by local paths; the scoped 3.0 graph is not a complete cross-workbook identity store.
scope: Persist hashes and source-qualified fields, references, diagnostics and local/server provenance with schema migrations.
Update changed/deleted/moved workbooks incrementally and join published lineage only when stable IDs/evidence exist.
acceptance: Incremental and clean rebuild results agree after edits, deletes and renames, with no stale dependency edges.
Duplicate captions and local/published copies retain distinct identities; optional metadata joins expose uncertainty.
Queries cover fields, custom SQL, connections and transitive affected workbooks; index version upgrades and concurrent reads are tested.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Add governed publish/promotion plans with revision checks and recovery
items.baseline: Publish/download/refresh workflows exist; they do not constitute a complete reviewed, revision-safe promotion transaction.
scope: Prepare a dry-run deployment plan with source/output hashes, semantic/governance checks, permission prerequisites and intended server/site/project IDs.
Use conditional revision guards only where upstream supports them; otherwise disclose the preflight/publish race and required coordination. Persist job outcomes and define safe compensating rollback.
acceptance: Changed inputs or observed remote revision changes abort preflight. Tests distinguish upstream conditional publishing from best-effort check/write behavior and document any race window.
Tests cover async failure, unknown publish outcome, permissions, retry duplication, rollback conflicts and multi-workbook partial success.
Examples document explicit approval boundaries and downloadable recovery artifacts; no operation claims global server atomicity.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Add bounded-memory multi-table extract evolution and refresh
items.baseline: Real Hyper query/upsert/rolling refresh and contract validation exist. DataFrame-based paths and contract writes are not a general streaming multi-table transaction planner.
scope: Design batch/Arrow or iterable ingestion with exact contract validation and bounded-memory key checking.
Plan multi-table schema evolution, refresh windows and provenance while preserving unrelated tables and workbook XML contracts.
acceptance: Benchmark memory and throughput on realistic extracts; published limits include duplicate/null composite keys and exact numeric/time semantics.
Failure injection leaves original extracts/XML intact across supported multi-table writes.
Streaming and in-memory results agree; unsupported type coercions and raw external extract handles remain explicit.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Validate performance telemetry adapters and evidence-based correlation
items.baseline: Complexity scoring exists; #104 remains open and has no implemented performance_correlation API. Its old draft conflated Cloud Admin Insights with Server repository telemetry.
scope: Start with anonymized, user-supplied telemetry exports and stable workbook/sheet/query identity plus timestamp/timezone normalization.
Evaluate distinct optional Cloud Admin Insights and Server repository/performance-recording adapters against documented permissions and schema availability.
acceptance: Publish a reproducible spike on representative telemetry, including unmatched rows, missing data, confidence and sample-window limits.
Report correlations and candidate bottlenecks without asserting calculated-field causation from workbook complexity alone.
Document platform-specific access/freshness limits and a go/no-go decision for production adapters; no invented REST endpoint.
items.exclude: Admin Insights is a Tableau Cloud feature. Do not require three recommendations regardless of available evidence or promise a causal optimizer.

items.title: Research evidence-backed XML transforms and compatibility profiles
items.baseline: 3.0 has a conservative capability registry and guarded header migrations; it does not implement arbitrary XML downgrade conversion.
scope: Select one bounded feature/version transition with paired native before/after fixtures and documented information-loss rules.
Prototype a transform registry with dry-run compatibility evidence, custom rules and rollback.
acceptance: Publish paired native save/reopen evidence and semantic diffs for the chosen transition.
Unknown XML/features stay unverified; unsupported or lossy conversion requires explicit decisions and does not silently succeed.
Produce a go/no-go and separately scoped implementation proposal; breaking semantics require a new major version.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Research Git-friendly normalization and three-way patch conflict handling
items.baseline: Snapshot patches preserve complete target XML/assets with strict fingerprints. Existing git_clean has a separate P0 style-preservation correction in R30. Neither operation provides general three-way merge or compact-delta patches.
scope: Prototype opt-in source-control views and base/local/remote conflict reports using stable identities and native ordering evidence.
Measure compact asset delta/storage approaches with licensing, payload and secret-redaction constraints.
acceptance: Round-trip fixtures prove any normalization preserves meaning and order-sensitive XML; original source remains recoverable.
Conflicts include unknown XML and assets and cannot be silently auto-resolved.
Compare reviewability/storage against snapshots and issue a go/no-go before defining a new patch format.
items.exclude: No automatic alphabetical XML sorting, thumbnail stripping or semantic ID rewriting without evidence and an explicit opt-in.

items.title: Evaluate optional event-driven and ecosystem workflow adapters
items.baseline: Core local workflows and thin TSC integration exist. The project has no committed general event automation or external platform adapter contract.
scope: Identify concrete consumer requests for webhook/event, Migration SDK, orchestration or agent-tool adapters.
Prototype a single optional adapter using explicit approved operations, replay IDs and the publish/migration plan contracts.
acceptance: Design records name the consumer, supported upstream API/license and stable local interface.
Replay, authorization, malformed payload and unavailable integration cases are tested without side-effectful discovery.
Keep core dependent only on lxml; choose go/no-go and a separately scoped implementation issue.
items.exclude: No hosted service, full REST API clone, mandatory orchestrator/AI dependency or unrequested external communication.

items.title: Publish typed API contracts, support policy and upgrade documentation
items.baseline: Configured mypy checks pass, but pyproject has module-level ignore_errors overrides and several dynamic integration/report types. That is not universal strict typing.
scope: Inventory public APIs, remove type-check exemptions incrementally and publish stable errors/report schemas and deprecation policy.
Improve API reference and cookbook coverage for 2.x-to-3.x transitions, optional dependencies and exact save/transaction/version semantics.
acceptance: Typed consumer examples and contract tests cover each declared stable API without suppressing their own errors.
A support table names Python, dependency floors, OS/architecture and Tableau capability evidence with unverified cases.
Docs link runnable examples, backward-compatible changes and major-version triggers; exported symbols and annotations are checked in CI.
items.exclude: No unrelated library rewrite or expansion into a general Tableau administration platform.

items.title: Reject unsafe existing merge cases before mutation and honor conflicts
items.baseline: Workbook.merge() copies XML collections with simple name suffixes. It does not reconcile imported references/assets and does not forward its public conflict_suffix to the collection helper.
scope: Audit the existing merge entry point and reject collision/asset/unsupported cases it cannot safely preserve.
Honor the current conflict parameter, avoid duplicate generated names and preserve destination state on every rejection.
acceptance: Negative tests cover same datasource/sheet IDs, repeated suffix collisions, dependent references and owned assets.
Safe supported existing merges retain valid dependencies and save/reopen; unsafe inputs fail before changing XML/assets.
Document the intentionally limited patch-safe contract and link the full reconciliation API follow-up R05.
items.exclude: No new dry-run or reconciliation API in a patch release; broader native merging is R05 in 3.1.

items.title: Fix destructive git_clean style removal and preserve semantic content
items.baseline: The shipped xml.canonical.git_clean removes every //style block; native FormatSpec stores font/color formats there. Workbook and CLI cleaning overwrite their source. A scratch reproduction confirms the loss.
scope: Preserve native style rules and unknown semantic XML; remove only evidenced volatile metadata while retaining full document comments/PIs and order.
Make writes transactional and ensure dry-run/non-in-place operation cannot change source files.
acceptance: Regression fixtures retain font, number, color and inherited style rules after cleaning and save/reopen.
Tests cover unknown XML, pre/post-root comments/PIs, entity safety, malformed input and write failure without source loss.
The existing API and CLI clearly document normalization behavior; new optional normalization policies require a minor release.
items.exclude: Do not treat all styles as volatile. New compact/three-way patch design remains separate research in R26.
